Not ready for a PR: `app/routes.py` fails on import because `db` doesn't exist anywhere, and the endpoint misses both the ordering and the 50-row cap its spec row requires.

Reviewed: uncommitted working tree · 1 file, 11 changed lines · spec: `TODO_WORKFLOW.md:10` (row 1.2)
Agents: planned 7 reviewers + up to 8 verifiers · spawned 7 + 8
Not reviewed: nothing was run end to end, because Flask and SQLAlchemy aren't installed here and the models are placeholders. The N+1 and missing-item findings rest on documented SQLAlchemy behaviour, not a run. One reviewer nit about the module-level `app` object (`app/routes.py:5`) was dropped unverified because that line is outside the diff.

## Spec
- missing · `app/routes.py:10` · "newest first" · add an `order_by` descending; `Order` has no timestamp yet, so it needs a sort column first (or `Order.id.desc()` if ids are monotonic).
- missing · `app/routes.py:10` · "at most 50 per response" · add `.limit(50)` before `.all()`.

## Blockers
- `app/routes.py:2` · `from app import db` raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'db' from 'app'` (reproduced); there is no `app/__init__.py` and nothing defines `db` · create `db` in `app/__init__.py` and bind the models to it.
- `app/routes.py:10` · `Order.query` is `None` (`app/models.py:3`), so the first request raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'filter_by'` (reproduced with the import stubbed) · make `Order` and `Item` real mapped models before this endpoint lands.
- `app/routes.py:8-10` · no authentication and no ownership check, so any caller can read any user's orders by changing the path id; nothing in the repo adds auth or declares it out of scope · require auth and compare the caller to `user_id`, or add an explicit auth row to `TODO_WORKFLOW.md` before this is exposed.

## Should-fix
- `app/routes.py:12-13` · N+1: one `Item` lookup per order, with no relationship, eager load or cache to avoid it. Repeated item ids don't reliably help, because the identity map holds weak references and `item` is rebound each iteration · fetch in one query, e.g. join `Order` to `Item` and select `Order.id, Item.name`.
- `app/routes.py:14` · `.get()` returns `None` for a NULL or dangling `item_id`, so `item.name` raises and one bad row turns the whole list into a 500; there is no FK constraint or error handler · the join above makes this explicit (inner join skips, outer join returns `item_name: null`); pick one.
- `app/routes.py:8-15` / `tests/test_routes.py:1-2` · the endpoint has no tests at all, not just the zero-orders case; the only test is `assert True` and never imports `app.routes`, which is why the import failure goes unnoticed · add test-client tests for zero orders (200, `[]`), the happy path, 51+ orders, and a missing item.

## Nits
- `app/routes.py:13` · `Query.get()` is legacy, superseded by `Session.get()`; it still works in SQLAlchemy 2.x but warns on every call (no version is pinned in the repo) · moot if the join replaces it, otherwise use `db.session.get(Item, order.item_id)`.

## Needs validation
- String `user_id` compared against a possibly integer column · `app/routes.py:8` · missing fact: the declared type of `Order.user_id` and the database backend (the real model or migration, once written). On PostgreSQL a non-numeric id against an integer column would be a 500; on SQLite it silently returns `[]`.
- No index supporting the `user_id` filter · `app/routes.py:10` · missing fact: whether the real `orders` table has an index leading with `user_id` (the model or migration, or `\d orders` in the database).

## What's solid
- Response shape matches the spec: a JSON list of `{order_id, item_name}`, filtered to the given user.
- Zero orders: by reading, the loop is skipped and the handler returns `[]` with a 200 once the query works; it is only untested.
- Simplicity: no issues. The one suggestion raised (swap to `Item.query.get` and drop the import) was refuted, since it fails on the placeholder models and keeps the legacy call.

I haven't changed anything. If you want these fixed, I can implement the ranked list, or you can run `/code-review --fix`.
